title: Drying, Water Activity, Packaging and Storage Stability
summary: Post-harvest quality continues to change after cutting; drying, water activity, oxygen, light, temperature, packaging and time must be controlled and measured as a connected stability system.

sections.title: Drying is heat and mass transfer
sections.body: Temperature, humidity, airflow, product dimensions and loading affect how water leaves harvested flowers. Average room conditions do not guarantee that product at different positions or flower sizes reaches the same moisture state at the same time.

sections.title: Moisture content and water activity differ
sections.body: Moisture content describes how much water is present, while water activity relates to the availability of water for microbial growth and chemical reactions. Similar moisture contents can therefore have different stability implications depending on product structure and distribution.

sections.title: Storage effects are product- and condition-specific
sections.body: Time, temperature, light, oxygen and packaging barrier properties can affect cannabinoids and volatile compounds. Modified-atmosphere research illustrates that preserving one compound or class does not prove universal preservation of all cannabinoids and aromatics.
